short: Two years, a disputed usurpation, and the last English king to die in battle.
full:
Richard, Duke of Gloucester, had served his brother Edward IV loyally in the north for a decade. When Edward died in April 1483 he took custody of the twelve-year-old Edward V, had the boy and his brother declared illegitimate on the grounds of a precontracted marriage, and was crowned on 6 July. The princes were last seen in the Tower that summer; their fate remains unresolved.

His reign lasted twenty-six months. Buckingham's rebellion in October 1483 failed, but it left Henry Tudor as the focus of exiled opposition, and the deaths of Richard's son and wife in 1484-85 weakened him further. On 22 August 1485 he met Henry at Bosworth, charged the enemy standard in person, and was killed when the Stanleys held back their troops and then turned on him. He was buried without ceremony at Leicester, where his remains were found under a car park in 2012.
